clauses.reason: The lead finds that the situation in and in relation to Syria undermines the campaign against ISIS, endangers civilians and threatens peace, security and stability in the region and so constitutes an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security and foreign policy of the United States, declares a national emergency to deal with it and orders what follows. On 2026-10-14 the clause is operative: the emergency it rests on was continued by the notice of 2026-09-30. The clause continues, amended: before 14142 the finding named recent actions by the Government of Turkey; after it that phrase is struck and the rest is unchanged; Executive Order 14312 then expands the emergency's scope without restating the lead. Executive Order 14312 does not revoke or supersede the order, and the order states no end date.

clauses.mechanism: express_strike: Executive Order 14142 section 1(b) strikes section 1(a)(i)(B)-(F) and inserts two replacement criteria that do not carry the Turkey-related criteria
clauses.reason: Section 1(a)(i)(B), (C) and (D) block persons who are current or former officials of the Government of Turkey, subdivisions, agencies or instrumentalities of that Government, and persons operating in sectors of the Turkish economy determined by the Secretary of the Treasury. Executive Order 14142 section 1(b), dated January 15, 2025, strikes subsections 1(a)(i)(B)-(F) and inserts in lieu thereof two criteria (assisting a blocked person; being owned or controlled by or acting for a blocked person) that restate section 1(a)(i)(E)-(F) and do not restate the Turkey-related criteria; the order states no separate effective date, so it took effect on signing on 2025-01-15. The Turkey-related criteria therefore ended on that date by express striking, and on 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated. No earlier ending is shown: the Treasury notice of 2020 unblocked named persons individually and did not strike the criteria. Any person still blocked under another criterion is not affected.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13894 of October 14, 2019 (84 FR 55851), Blocking Property and Suspending Entry of Certain Persons Contributing to the Situation in Syria, declares a national emergency and has twelve sections. The held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13894.txt, 84 FR 55851, PDF pages 1-5) carries the heading, the date October 14, 2019 and FR Doc. 2019-22849. The dossier's inventory omits the preamble sentence that finds the threat and declares the national emergency and orders ('I hereby declare a national emergency to deal with that threat. I hereby determine and order:'), and splits the paragraphs of section 1(a)(i) and section 2 into machine fragments (including repeated 'dup' scopes), so the inventory is corrected to 25 clauses with exact spans: the lead; section 1(a) with its (i)(A), (i)(B)-(D) and (i)(E)-(F) criteria and 1(b); section 2(a) to (d); section 3(a) to (c); and sections 4 to 12. Two later orders amend the order. Executive Order 14142 (January 15, 2025) strikes a phrase about Turkey from the second paragraph, strikes section 1(a)(i)(B)-(F) and inserts two new criteria (assisting a blocked person; being owned or controlled by or acting for a blocked person), and strikes section 8(f), the definition of Government of Turkey. Executive Order 14312 (June 30, 2025) expands the scope of the emergency and strikes and restates section 1(a) and section 2(a). Under the owner ruling on strike-and-insert amendments, clauses so amended continue, amended, with the amendment recorded as a later event; a clause struck without replacement ends on the date of the striking order. On that basis the Turkey-related criteria in section 1(a)(i)(B)-(D) and the definition in section 8(f) are terminated by Executive Order 14142 on 2025-01-15; the other clauses are operative on 2026-10-14. The emergency was continued by the notice of September 30, 2026. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13894 (32 files) finds the order, Executive Orders 14142 and 14312, the annual notices, State and Treasury notices and rules and 31 CFR part 569; the only wording that ends anything is the 2025 amendments. The held text is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF; page images were not inspected. The substance of section 1(a) and section 2(a) changed in 2025 and the later events mark that for the reviewer.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states no end date, event or condition. The held annual continuation notices of 2020 to 2026 continue the emergency; none terminates it. The held-corpus number search found two ending events, both amendments by later presidential orders: Executive Order 14142 (2025-01-15), whose strikings end the clauses listed above, and Executive Order 14312 (2025-06-30), which restates sections 1(a) and 2(a) without ending them. Earlier events do not end the Turkey-related clauses: the Treasury notice of 2020 unblocking named Turkish officials removes persons from the list (individual delistings) and is not an act of the President striking the criteria. The Department of State notices of 2020 designate persons and end nothing. The OFR catalog, U.S. Code and CFR searches record no revocation of the order.","independent_command_check":"The independent commands are the declaration of emergency; the blocking command and its criteria groups; the exception clauses in 1(b), 2(d) and 3(c); the sanctions authority in section 2(a) and the procurement/visa and financial sanctions of 2(b) and 2(c); the foreign-financial-institution authority of section 3; the entry suspension of section 4; the donations determination of section 5; the inclusion rules of section 6; the evasion and conspiracy prohibitions of section 7; the definitions of section 8 (with 8(f) separate); the no-prior-notice determination of section 9; the delegation of section 10; the report authority of section 11; and the general provisions of section 12.","savings_check":"Two clauses (section 1(a)(i)(B)-(D) and section 8(f)) are terminated; the savings reason states what survives. The other clauses continue, amended where a later event is recorded.","scope_check":"Clauses are decided separately: the Turkey-related criteria (section 1(a)(i)(B)-(D)) and the definition of Government of Turkey (section 8(f)) were struck by Executive Order 14142 without replacement; the assistance and ownership criteria (section 1(a)(i)(E)-(F)) were replaced by new criteria (B) and (C) with the same content; section 1(a) and section 2(a) were restated by Executive Order 14312; the remaining clauses are untouched."}

savings.reason: Designations made under the struck Turkey-related criteria were removed or are individually managed by the Treasury's lists; the held notice of February 2020 unblocks named Turkish persons designated under section 1(a)(i)(B). Nothing held transfers the struck clauses elsewhere, and the surviving criteria and sanctions continue independently under the order as amended.
